cultivar: Local population cultivars and other suitable varieties
processing: Green tea from one bud with one leaf, or one bud with a just-opening second leaf, finished into a single round ball of 18 to 20 mm weighing about 2.5 g.
harvest_season: Spring. Pickings are one bud with one leaf or a barely opened second leaf; local accounts tie the tea's quality to overwintered buds developing around Qingming.
appearance_dry: A neat sphere 18 to 20 mm across with a silvery grey, dark green surface.
appearance_liquor: Not closely described; a clear yellow-green is typical of a Guizhou spring green.
appearance_wet: The ball slowly loosens over about three minutes and opens out in the cup like a bud unfolding.
taste_profile: A clean, refreshing aroma with a rich, mellow body, a brisk mouthfeel and a sweet return.

brewing.notes: The traditional serving is one ball of about 2.5 g in a glass with 150 ml of boiling water, left for about three minutes while it opens. A clear glass is the point. Later steep times are a suggestion.

vintage_note: Sold as a spring green, normally by the current year's harvest. Like other greens it is best within a year. Producers also sell a tianma-blended version, which is a different product from the plain ball.
description:
Leishan Yinqiu, silver ball tea, is a green tea from Leishan county in southeast Guizhou, and its shape is the whole introduction: each portion is one round ball about 2 cm across, one per cup. It has national geographical indication status, and it is one of the teas usually named among Guizhou's best known.

The ball is built from young spring leaf, one bud with one or two leaves, and comes out silvery grey over dark green. The protected area covers nine townships of Leishan county, using local population plants and other suitable varieties.

This is a tea to watch. Drop a ball into a glass, pour on boiling water and give it about three minutes: it slowly loosens and the leaf opens out. The cup is clean and fresh with a rich body and sweet finish. Boiling water is unusually hot for a green, but a tight ball needs it to open.

When buying, look for an even, tight ball and a clear harvest date. As with other greens, the current year is what you want. Producers around the county make several other teas too, so check that the packet says Yinqiu and not a blended or flavoured version, unless that is what you are after.

Selenium is part of the marketing, with a claimed 2.00 to 2.02 micrograms per gram. It is a local figure, and the shape and freshness are better reasons to try it.
history:
The tea dates from the early 1980s, which makes it a modern creation rather than an old tribute tea. It collected honours soon after: a Ministry of Light Industry quality title in 1986 and a gold award at the first China food expo in 1988, and it was chosen as a Foreign Ministry gift in 1991.

Later awards include a special gold at the Shanghai tea expo in 2011. In September 2014 the national quality authority approved geographical indication protection, covering nine townships of Leishan county.
